title: Locus Coeruleus Tractography and Pupillometric Reactivity for the Investigation of Multiple Sclerosis-Associated Fatigue
summary:
Background:
Many people with multiple sclerosis experience pronounced and persistent exhaustion that can significantly affect everyday life. The exact causes of this exhaustion are not yet fully understood. There is evidence that certain areas of the brain involved in attention, wakefulness and readiness to perform may play a role. Changes in pupil size and in nerve connections within the brain may provide indications of altered function in these brain areas in the patient group being studied.
Research question:
The study aims to investigate whether pupil responses differ between people with multiple sclerosis and healthy individuals and whether these differences are related to experienced exhaustion. In addition, the study will investigate whether people with multiple sclerosis show changes in certain nerve connections in the brain and whether these changes are also related to exhaustion.
Methods:
Participants complete various questionnaires and perform simple tasks while listening to sequences of tones. During these tasks, pupil size is recorded using a camera. Participants with multiple sclerosis additionally undergo brain imaging in a magnetic resonance scanner to examine the structure and connections of different brain regions. The data obtained are then compared with the level of exhaustion reported in the questionnaires. For comparison of the brain imaging data, existing research data from healthy individuals available in public databases are also used.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For all participants:
Native German speaker

For patients with multiple sclerosis:
Diagnosis of definite multiple sclerosis according to the 2024 McDonald diagnostic criteria; normal cognitive screening result (Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score > 21 points).
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for participation in pupillometry:
Neurological or psychiatric pre-existing conditions (except multiple sclerosis); current exacerbation of multiple sclerosis (relapse within the past 4 weeks); corticosteroid pulse therapy within the past 4 weeks; pregnancy (verbal confirmation of non-pregnancy is sufficient); use of centrally acting medications (except multiple sclerosis medication) according to the table by Kelbsch et al., 2019; relevant ocular conditions (including previous eye surgery, glaucoma, pseudoexfoliation syndrome at the pupillary margin or lens, corneal disease, non-spheroidal pupils, or relevant anisocoria), diabetes mellitus;  multifocal contact lenses, reflective glasses, or glasses with highly reflective jewelry (if these can be removed and visual acuity remains sufficient to fixate on the fixation cross, participants may still be included and the measurement will be performed without the respective visual aid)

Exclusion criteria for participation in tractography:
General exclusion criteria for magnetic resonance imaging (metal implants, claustrophobia, and tattoos larger than the palm of the hand)
